Fixed 54-contract Heston · noise-scale development

One Gaussian scale: assumptions, joint inference and measured checks

Fixed-scale sensitivity and an inferred-scale posterior answer different questions. All predeclared checkpoints and unresolved references remain visible.

TargetsCalibration vs informationFixed sensitivityJoint scaleTrainingConditional checksPopulationRecoverySource codeSources

Same observations, two inference questions

Yᵢ = Pᵢ(φ) + c hᵢ Zᵢ,   Zᵢ ∼ N(0,1)Known frozen half-spreads h; one shared scale c. Conditional quote errors are independent.

Fixed c=.5,1,2 changes the assumed likelihood at identical observed prices. Joint inference instead learns six targets: five physical Heston parameters and c∼Uniform(.5,2). The generating c is never an input; the estimator receives only 54 ordered Y/h values.

The known-scale physical MAP is unchanged by global c rescaling under the fixed Uniform physical prior, but posterior means and widths can change. Joint physical marginals use p(c|y), not an unweighted average of fixed-scale curves. Half-spread-as-SD and the c prior remain conventions.

The old 63 grid was symmetric at 20%; the current 54 is already put-heavy and remains frozen here. The audited E63 proposal adds short-expiry/wing coverage but lacks a full-year PM expiry and its original final +2 call. No grid repricing, spread-profile change, tau component or Bergomi work enters this study.

Explicit reference environment recovery

The report follows the separately hash-bound recovery addendum and recovered reference protocol. The original study and original reference protocol remain bound and preserved; this is not a silent change of observations, targets or priors.

Calibration does not establish information learning

SBC calibration is different from learning information.

A predictor that ignores the quotes and returns the prior can pass marginal prior-predictive SBC. Near-prior c intervals therefore need to be read with recovery and matched conditional references. Neural ignorance does not establish that c is unidentified by the model.

Updatesc median RMSEConstant prior-median RMSETruth–median correlationMedian posterior 90% width / prior 90% width
10,0000.442140.43707-0.00681.3460 / 1.3500 = 0.997×
50,0000.44820.43707-0.06091.3368 / 1.3500 = 0.990×
60,0000.44520.43707-0.04811.3362 / 1.3500 = 0.990×

The constant baseline always predicts the Uniform-prior median 1.25 on these same truths. A width ratio near 1 indicates little interval contraction in the neural output; it is not a pass/fail criterion. Correct posterior medians need not be Uniform, and perfect recovery is not expected from noisy observations. Ready joint MCMC establishes the conditional target; this table alone cannot diagnose model identifiability.

A narrow joint-reference c posterior alongside a near-prior neural posterior is a case-specific approximation failure: the specified data/model contain information the estimator misses. It is not global non-identifiability. These comparisons concern the full joint marginal, unlike the known-physical oracle.

Unknown-c physical marginals integrate over the data-dependent posterior p(c|y). They are not an equal mixture of the three fixed-scale curves. The old c=1 neural estimator is not used at c=.5 or 2.

Joint scale versus a known-physical oracle

The joint reference infers physical parameters and c together. The fixed-physical oracle instead conditions on the saved generating parameters. Its interval is not a replacement reference for the joint marginal.

CaseJoint marginal c · q05/median/q95Fixed-generating-physical oracle · q05/median/q95
Broad synthetic[0.93811, 1.0974, 1.3152][0.92503, 1.07739, 1.27659]
Market-like synthetic[0.9702, 1.1406, 1.3645][1.0119, 1.17855, 1.39646]
Actual market[1.9971, 1.9993, 2]No known market truth

Prior support is [.5,2]. Undefined correlations are omitted, not replaced by zero. Small Pearson correlations do not establish independence: scale–width dependence can remain without linear correlation.

Posterior pressure near c=2 can reflect insufficient residual-scale support, model discrepancy or data/prior conditions. It does not identify pure measurement noise or authorize retrospective prior expansion. Market scale has no generating truth.

Training recipe and objective

The 10k/50k/60k checkpoints are predeclared. Probe loss uses the trainer's learned target coordinates; no physical-density ranking is inferred. Five-target and six-target NLLs have different dimensions and are not an accuracy ranking.

The spline uses six coupling blocks and 128×128 conditioners. Construction uses dropout .05, then 24 existing layers are switched to effective dropout 0 before the first update without changing state arrays. Adam moments are retained at rate changes. The source below shows the executing code.

Neural versus matched joint references

Reference readiness requires four-chain rank-normalized R-hat ≤1.01 and bulk/tail ESS ≥400 for the parameters and two variance products, plus sampled numerical price refinement within .02×(.5h)=.01h, independently of inferred c. These sampled checks are not a prior-wide pricing certificate. A ready reference can still reveal a neural approximation error.

Same-target neural mean error must be at most .3 reference SD and its central-90% width ratio must lie in [.75,1.25], with Monte Carlo uncertainty and the predeclared 144-check family accounted for. Each endpoint retains both synthetic cases and the separate market application. Within each case, 16 individual checks cover mean and width for six parameters plus two analytic variance quantities. Their Monte Carlo intervals are not posterior credible intervals.

The predeclared terminal endpoint, 60k, appears first; it was not selected as the best result. The earlier 10k and 50k tables remain below in expandable sections, and all tables are included when printing.

Final 60k recovery, including c

All 512 medians; 32 marginal 90% intervals selected by fixed row index, not outcome. Bars are posterior intervals, not Monte Carlo error bars. Full-prior plots can look excellent despite material local conditional errors.

Detail view of exactly the same 32 cases. Vertical scales vary by parameter and use physical units.

Posterior-median ECDF is not expected to be Uniform under exact inference; this is descriptive recovery. SBC uses posterior ranks, not the distribution of medians.

Executed network, augmentation and learning-rate code

Exact AST-extracted functions from the hash-bound executed trainer; the module is not imported or run. The construction rate .05 is followed by the separately verified 24-layer zero-dropout switch.

build_workflow
def build_workflow(task):
    validate_task(task)
    import bayesflow as bf
    import keras
    if bf.__version__ != "2.1.0" or keras.backend.backend() != "jax":
        raise RuntimeError("locked BF2.1 JAX environment required")
    adapter = bf.Adapter()
    for name,(lo,hi) in zip(task["target"]["parameter_names"],task["target"]["prior_bounds"],strict=True):
        adapter = adapter.constrain(name,lower=float(lo),upper=float(hi),inclusive="none")
    adapter = (adapter.convert_dtype("float64","float32")
        .concatenate(task["target"]["parameter_names"],into="inference_variables")
        .concatenate(["observations"],into="inference_conditions"))
    optimizer = keras.optimizers.Adam(keras.optimizers.schedules.CosineDecay(5e-4,10000,alpha=.1))
    flow = bf.networks.CouplingFlow(transform="spline",depth=6,subnet_kwargs={"widths":[128,128],"dropout":.05})
    workflow = bf.BasicWorkflow(adapter=adapter,inference_network=flow,
        standardize=["inference_variables","inference_conditions"],optimizer=optimizer)
    workflow.estimator.compile(optimizer=optimizer,steps_per_execution=1)
    return workflow
augmented_batch
def augmented_batch(clean,physical,halfspread,step,seed,*,namespace=0):
    clean,physical,h = np.asarray(clean),np.asarray(physical),np.asarray(halfspread)
    if clean.ndim != 2 or physical.shape != (len(clean),5) or h.shape != (clean.shape[1],):
        raise ValueError("matching clean prices, five physical labels and frozen quote spreads required")
    c = draw_c(len(clean),step,seed,namespace=namespace)
    # Identical Gaussian namespace to the fixed-c recipe, independent of c's stream.
    error = np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence([NOISE_NAMESPACE,seed,namespace,step])).standard_normal(clean.shape)
    quotes = clean+c[:,None]*h*error
    return quotes,np.column_stack((physical,c))
draw_c
def draw_c(count,step,seed,*,namespace=0):
    return np.random.default_rng(np.random.SeedSequence([SCALE_NAMESPACE,seed,namespace,step])).uniform(.5,2.,size=count)
install_annealing
def install_annealing(model,state):
    """Only replace a built-in schedule; preserve all Adam/model arrays."""
    import keras
    fixed.assign_state(model,state)
    before = fixed.state_summary(model,fixed.current_state(model))
    old = model.optimizer.get_config()
    if (int(model.optimizer.iterations.numpy())!=50000
            or old["learning_rate"]["class_name"]!="CosineDecay"
            or old["learning_rate"]["config"]["decay_steps"]!=10000):
        raise ValueError("joint annealing must begin at absolute50000 with the original cosine schedule")
    model.optimizer.learning_rate = keras.optimizers.schedules.PiecewiseConstantDecay(
        [54999],[5e-6,5e-7],name="heston_spread_two_stage_annealing")
    after = fixed.state_summary(model,fixed.current_state(model))
    new = model.optimizer.get_config()
    if before != after or {k:v for k,v in old.items() if k!="learning_rate"}!={k:v for k,v in new.items() if k!="learning_rate"}:
        raise RuntimeError("annealing reset saved arrays or other Adam configuration")
    return {"absolute_step":50000,"old_schedule":old["learning_rate"],"new_schedule":new["learning_rate"],
            "all_array_hashes_unchanged":True}

The effective zero-dropout action

This exact call occurs in run_training before the first native optimizer update:

toggle = fixed.switch_dropout_zero(model)
Frozen helper: switch_dropout_zero
def switch_dropout_zero(model, *, reloading=False):
    """Change only existing Dropout rates after original .05 initialization."""
    layers = dropout_layers(model)
    rates = [float(layer.rate) for layer in layers]
    if len(layers) != 24 or any(rate not in ((0., .05) if reloading else (.05,)) for rate in rates):
        raise ValueError("zero-dropout control requires the frozen 24-layer .05 construction")
    before = state_summary(model, current_state(model))
    for layer in layers:
        layer.rate = 0.
    after = state_summary(model, current_state(model))
    if before != after:
        raise RuntimeError("changing dropout rates changed learned/permutation/optimizer/standardizer/RNG arrays")
    return {"method": "construct/build original .05 model, then change existing Dropout.rate to0 before the first update",
            "rates_before": rates, "rates_after": [float(layer.rate) for layer in layers],
            "array_state_unchanged": True,
            "state_groups": {name: {"variable_count": len(rows), "before_sha256": fingerprint(rows),
                                    "after_sha256": fingerprint(after[name])} for name, rows in before.items()},
            "original_initial_full_hash_available": False,
            "claim_limit": "exact within-replay before/after equality; original default run did not persist its full initial state",
            "archive_scope": "network constructor remains .05; load_checkpoint reapplies recorded effective zero rates; exact training resume unsupported"}
